name: NBC CSO Alarm Map live outfall status (JSON)
waters_covered: NBC district urban rivers: Providence, Woonasquatucket, Moshassuck, West, Seekonk, Blackstone (Pawtucket/Central Falls)
access_detail: GET https://cso-api.narrabay.com/pins, no auth, returns JSON array (67 rows on 2026-11-01, 26 KB; IIS/ASP.NET). Called by the Leaflet map on https://www.narrabay.com/programs-and-initiatives/combined-sewer-overflow-cso/cso-alarm-map/ . Map colours: HoursSinceLast<=24 red, <=48 orange, else grey. No other paths found (/, /swagger, /history etc. return 404).

sample_record.SITE_NOTES: 56" opening in chamber followed by net screening before discharging to the Moshassuck River near the intersection of Moshassuck St and Esten Ave, Pawtucket

cadence: Live alarm feed from NBC's flow/level monitoring (Telog). Page JS has a disabled 60 s refresh; NBC 2022 launch note says overflows show 'as they occur' and stay visible up to 48 hours. On the check date every ACTIVATION_DATE was null (no overflow in the window).
history: None in this endpoint (only the latest activation per site within the window). Archive must be built by polling.
legal_basis: RIPDES permits RI0100315/RI0100072 (2017): NBC must 'develop a system to provide web-based notification to the public on CSO occurrences' (DEM release 2017-10-04).
status_reason: Only real-time, machine-readable, outfall-level sewage discharge feed in Rhode Island; best first build target.
notes: Timezone of ACTIVATION_DATE not stated; map code applies moment.utcOffset('4') before display, so the stored value may be UTC or local - confirm with a live event. 10 of 60 CSO sites carry 'No data available' (no live alarm). Includes a demo row 'OF 000 WBNS Test 2024' and a blank row (SITE_ID 0) to filter out.

name: NBC 'Verified Overflow Events in the last 30 Days' (JSON)
access_detail: GET, no auth, JSON array; rendered as the table 'Verified Overflow Events in the last 30 Days' on the CSO Alarm Map page. On 2026-11-01 it held one row (OF 220, 2026-10-05). The endpoint name suggests dry-weather overflows; ECHO classifies the same event as a dry-weather CSO.
cadence: Rows appear after NBC verification (here ~9 h after the event ended); rolling 30-day window.
status_reason: Gives verified start/end times that /pins drops after 48 h.
notes: Dates are SQL-Server-style strings ('Oct  5 2026  8:50PM'), no timezone.

status_reason: Context layer for the map; 'count' 217 meaning unknown.

notes: Projected ~98% overflow volume reduction and ~4 untreated overflow events/year after all phases. Pawtucket Tunnel excavation finished Feb 2024; in-service date not confirmed in sources found (targets cited 2026-2027).

name: EPA ECHO detailed facility reports - RI single-event violations and sewer overflow/bypass event totals
operator: U.S. EPA (data reported by RI permittees via NeT-SewerOverflow / ICIS-NPDES)
access_detail: GET per permit, no auth, JSON ~50 KB. Keys used: Results.CWASECompliance.Sources[].Violations[] (ViolationDesc, NPDESViolationId, QtrNValue = event date or date range) and Results.SBEEventTotals (annual counts and gallons, SortOrder 1/2). Fetched for 20 RI permits; summary in raw/echo-dfr-ri-summary.json.

CWASECompliance violation.ViolationDesc: Dry-weather CSO discharge to waters of the U.S. that may endanger health or the environment

cadence: ICIS-NPDES extract weekly-ish (SystemExtractDate 10/30/2026 on check). Event appears after the operator's 5-day NeT-SewerOverflow report and state review; lag days to weeks.
history: Rolling 13 quarters (from 07/2023) for violations; annual totals 2022-2026.
license: U.S. federal government data (public domain); ECHO asks users to cite it.
status_reason: Only public place where RI SSOs and bypasses outside the NBC map appear; confirmed against NBC (OF 220, 10/05/2026) and DEM (East Providence, 05/04/2026). Coordinate with the federal agent's ECHO work.
notes: Lists only events coded as violations (dry-weather CSOs, SSOs, unanticipated bypasses), not routine permitted wet-weather CSOs. RIDEM's NeT-SewerOverflow FAQ says 'How to View NETSEWEROVERFLOW Reports in ECHO - Coming Soon!' (rev. 11/16/23). SBE totals and violation lists do not always agree (e.g., East Providence 2026 shows '--').
